study type: Mixed-methods (Delphi consensus and prospective longitudinal cohort study for PROM validation)
exposure: Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal, operative vaginal, scheduled cesarean, nonscheduled cesarean)
outcome: Reliability of STORK (Cronbach α, interitem correlation, split-half reliability, floor/ceiling effects)
cohort: A total of 525 postpartum individuals across all delivery modes who completed surveys during their inpatient stay and at 2, 6, and 12 weeks postpartum in a multicenter US study.
finding: The Stanford Obstetric Recovery Checklist (STORK) was found to be a valid, reliable, and responsive measure of outpatient postpartum recovery in US individuals.
mod_finding: STORK demonstrated responsiveness across different delivery modes, with overall scores increasing from baseline to week 12 by 19% after spontaneous vaginal delivery, 31% after operative vaginal delivery, 27% after scheduled cesarean delivery, and 20% after nonscheduled cesarean delivery.
